title: Runtime Governance Implementation Reference
readerIntent: Implement or audit preview, request, approval, activation, audit, cleanup, rollback, lifecycle, and operational signals without creating a second configuration authority.
priorKnowledge: Read configuration, operational governance, security, and runtime topology journeys.
owner: nConfig owns static startup and process lifecycle; nDynamo governs supported runtime-mutable contracts; owning services apply changes
summary: Runtime governance changes only supported control-plane contracts through immutable reviewed intent, tenant-scoped authorization, owned activation services, safe evidence, and rollback while static layered configuration and secrets remain in their original authorities.

sections.heading: Authority map
items: nConfig discovers modules, selects topology, loads static layered properties, and owns the single process lifecycle/signal coordinator.
nDynamo owns the governed lifecycle for supported schema, router, property, schema-access-policy, class, and pipeline control-plane behavior.
nRouter owns route exposure, token type, permission, tenant resolution, and request enforcement for control-plane APIs.
The owning schema/router/property/class/pipeline service validates and applies an approved change and restores its prior snapshot.
BackOffice, MCP, CLI, AI tools, and administrative clients may call and present these contracts but never become configuration or mutation authorities.

sections.heading: Governed lifecycle
items: Preview is side-effect free and reports normalized changes, affected artifacts, warnings, dependencies, compatibility, and destructive risk.
Request stores tenant, type, target, canonical patch or reference, base revision, digest where required, requester, reason, correlation, preview, and policy state.
Approval or rejection records immutable intent and enforces configured separation of duties.
Activation revalidates tenant, actor separation, permission, digest, revision, target existence, policy, exposure, dependency, and provider readiness before calling the owner.
Success and failure append redacted correlated audit evidence; query projections never replace the authoritative activation record or owning runtime state.
Cleanup follows retention and legal/audit policy. Rollback restores the previous snapshot through the same owner and records a new governed transition.

sections.heading: Configuration-type rules
items: Static defaults remain in module source and config/properties.js; runtime governance does not become a second startup loader.
Dynamic properties reject secret-bearing paths and prototype-mutating keys. Secrets stay in approved external/secret-manager configuration.
Schema and schema-access-policy changes preserve governed merge, generated model/service, tenant, access, cache, event, transaction, and version contracts.
Router changes preserve exposure, HTTP semantics, controller/action, token class, permission, limits, cache, API metadata, and compatibility.
Dynamic class, pipeline, or execution changes remain behind explicit permissions and exposure categories and are unavailable by default in production-like topologies.
A new mutable type extends this lifecycle and owner map; it does not introduce a dedicated database endpoint or parallel activation state machine.

sections.heading: Lifecycle and observability
items: Governance activation stays off high-volume request paths and refreshes effective registries through existing owner services/events.
Required startup governance dependencies affect readiness; optional control-plane integrations recover asynchronously without delaying unrelated business traffic.
Correlate preview, request, decision, activation, propagation, audit, cleanup, rollback, and resulting health without logging protected values or unrestricted patches.
Monitor pending age, decision outcomes, digest/revision conflicts, activation duration/failure, propagation lag, cleanup backlog, rollback, repeated conflicts, and affected business indicators.
Backup governed persistence and owning state; verify restoration and rollback before high-risk changes.

sections.heading: Verification
items: Positive preview/request/approve/activate/audit/rollback and repeated idempotent behavior.

Unauthorized, wrong principal/token class, wrong tenant, actor-separation violation, patch substitution, stale revision, unknown type/target, sensitive/prototype path, disabled exposure, and invalid dependency.
Partial activation, propagation failure, restart, concurrent requests, cleanup/retention, backup/restore, rollback conflict, performance, and bounded telemetry.
Contract, integration, modular topology, security, upgrade, generated artifacts, documentation, and regression tests.
Fail closed when immutable intent, tenant, revision, digest, permission, policy, owner, audit, or rollback safety cannot be trusted.
